nodes.rationale: Raw (itsm_tickets) and translated (tickets) documents use exactly the same _id built from meshId and payload.key; upsert keeps a single raw and single translated on retries. _id is immutable so migration copies to a new DB with recalculated IDs.

nodes.label: executionRecordId vs storedTicketId vs ticketKey
nodes.rationale: Execution._id (executionRecordId) identifies each attempt; storedTicketId is the shared raw/translated _id; HTTP executionId is kept temporarily as alias of the execution record to avoid breaking consumers. Prevents interchangeable use of the two IDs.

nodes.label: Raw ticket lifecycle (persisted -> translated | failed)
nodes.rationale: Raw ticket saved as persisted, becomes translated after translated upsert, failed on mapping or later persistence failure; attachment or orchestrator failures do not downgrade a translated ticket. The received status is retired and migrated to persisted.

nodes.label: Orchestrator flat payload contract (rol, ticket_id, mesh_id, execution_id)
nodes.rationale: ticket_id is the Jira key, mesh_id comes from MESH_ID, execution_id is storedTicketId, rol comes from ORCHESTRATOR_ROLE (replaces INITIAL_ROL). Using Execution._id as execution_id was rejected because the contract demands the _id stored in itsm_tickets. Snake_case is confined to the external serializer.

nodes.rationale: Each valid delivery increments revision; if the job is processing the upsert only bumps revision and execution reference; on finish the worker compares claimedRevision with revision and returns to pending if it advanced.

nodes.rationale: Unique workerId claims an eligible or expired job setting status=processing, leaseOwner, leaseUntil, claimedRevision. Defaults: WORKER_CONCURRENCY 5, polling 1000 ms, lease 120000 ms, heartbeat 30000 ms; expired lease can be reclaimed by another replica.

nodes.label: Retry policy: five attempts with backoff 5s/30s/2m/10m/30m
nodes.rationale: After the fifth failure the job stays failed, the execution records the error and the translated ticket is neither deleted nor marked as integration failure.
